description: Neuralink patient plays video games with his mind. Brain-computer interfaces are consumer products now.
The neon-drenched streets of Shinjuku — indistinguishable from concept art.
AI-generated deepfakes now indistinguishable from reality. Identity is a question mark.
Five companies control most of what you see, buy, and think. They have more power than most governments.
Low-poly vehicles straight out of a PS1 fever dream are now real consumer products.
Cities deploy real-time facial recognition despite bans. Surveillance networks in every public space.
The gig economy is just day labor with an app. An algorithm decides if you eat this week.
Gene-edited babies: second known case confirmed. Designer humans are no longer hypothetical.
Robot dogs patrol corporate campuses and city streets. Fully autonomous. Armed with cameras.
Tech billionaire builds self-sustaining underground bunker city in New Zealand. The rich are preparing for the collapse they're causing.
Stacked living units stretching into infinity. Blade Runner called it — we just call it rent.
Smart refrigerators track your eating habits and share data with insurance companies. Your appliances work for corporations.
Brain implant translates neural signals directly into speech at 62 words per minute. The line between human and machine blurs.
Amazon workers tracked by AI every second of their shift. Bathroom breaks monitored. Time off task calculated to the second.
Cyberpunk was supposed to be a warning, not a roadmap.
